subject.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration

question: Should STRICT migration treat every post-CAST UNIQUE-key collision as an actionable fail-closed migration error, or should `openclaw doctor --fix` own an approved non-destructive recovery workflow?
rationale: The branch establishes a persisted-data recovery policy for ambiguous values. The mechanical scope can be expanded, but choosing automated recovery, quarantine, or mandatory manual cleanup is a maintainer-owned data-safety decision.

options.title: Fail closed with complete diagnostics
options.body: Preflight normalized collisions across primary and secondary UNIQUE keys, then fail atomically with the exact table/index and recovery guidance.

options.title: Design Doctor recovery
options.body: Define and document a non-destructive Doctor workflow for ambiguous collisions before allowing migration to alter those values automatically.

options.title: Keep primary-key-only scope
options.body: Accept generic SQLite errors for secondary UNIQUE collisions and document that only primary-key conflicts receive targeted guidance.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with complete diagnostics
recommendation.body: Preflight normalized collisions across primary and secondary UNIQUE keys, then fail atomically with the exact table/index and recovery guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged SQLite safety migration established the migration invariants and is the closest feature-history ownership signal.
